metadata.note: The Cincinnati, Indianapolis and Western and its predecessors: two routes, Hamilton OH - Connersville - Rushville - Indianapolis (98.2 mi) and Indianapolis - Decatur IL (152.7 mi) - Springfield IL (44.5 mi), plus the Sidell - Olney branch under the CI&W Railway. One feature per drawable span and operator (Rule 4 splits), all on the same traced geometry where routes coincide. The CH&D-operated era of Hamilton - Indianapolis (widened here to 1893-1906 plus the 1914 anchor) and the B&O era of both main routes (1927-1950, 1942-1950) live in cincinnati_hamilton_and_dayton_railway.geojson. This layer adds: Cincinnati and Indianapolis Junction 1870-1872 and CI&W Railroad 1915-1927 on Hamilton - Indianapolis; CI&W Hamilton - Cincinnati trackage 1915-1927; Indiana and Illinois Central 1874, Indianapolis, Decatur and Springfield 1878/1880-1884, Indianapolis, Decatur and Western 1893, CH&D 1902 and CI&W 1922 on Indianapolis - Decatur; CI&W Decatur - Springfield 1921; CH&D Ste. Marie - Alliance 1900.
metadata.ownership_split: Hamilton - Indianapolis: Cincinnati and Indianapolis Junction (to 2 Jan 1873 or 2 Jan 1878 - ICC conflict) -> CH&D as agent for the CH&I and then the CI&W Railway (CH&D file) -> CI&W Railroad own organization 1 Dec 1915 -> B&O 1927 (CH&D file). Indianapolis - Decatur: I&IC -> ID&S (Aug-Nov 1875) -> ID&W (Dec 1887 / Jan 1888) -> ID&W 1894 / Decatur & Eastern -> CH&D as agent (from 1895) -> CI&W Railroad 1 Dec 1915 -> B&O 1927 (CH&D file); each foreclosure successor is a separate company with its own colour, drawn only where a span is proven. Decatur - Springfield: CH&D (1902-15, not drawn) -> CI&W RR -> B&O (not drawn). Sidell - Olney: DO&OR -> CH&D for the ID&W (16 Dec 1898) -> Sidell & Olney (1915; CI&W-owned stock but separately operated - not CI&W colour). NOT splits: the 1902 CH&I + ID&W consolidation into the CI&W Railway; the CH&D lease 1905-1914 and receiverships; B&O stock control of the CH&D (1909); USRA 1918-1920; the B&O stock purchase of Jan 1926 (the split is the 1927 acquisition).
metadata.omitted: Not drawn, per the report's drawable fields: Decatur - Springfield CH&D era (1902-1915) and B&O era - no confirmed passenger year; Sidell - Olney beyond Ste. Marie - Alliance, the DO&OR's own era (1881 anchor at Advance) and the Sidell & Olney / Kansas & Sidell era (1926 Sidell - Kansas anchor) - other companies' rows; the pre-1867 College Corner - Rushville piece (1852; no evidence); Fowler's queried "Rogersville 1863AG here?"; the East Springfield yard tracks and the Indianapolis and Hamilton belt/yard trackage (freight). The Indianapolis & Cincinnati TRACTION interurban (Indianapolis - Rushville - Connersville) is a different company and is not part of this layer. The B&O era of Hamilton - Cincinnati is already drawn by bo-cincinnati-dayton (CH&D file).
metadata.freight_only_check: No freight-only years drawn. Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 59 HAMILTON AND INDIANAPOLIS and Table 60 INDIANAPOLIS AND SPRINGFIELD are "Freight Service only"; nothing here is drawn later than 1927, and no feature is drawn for the yard/belt trackage.
metadata.horsecar_check: None: steam from the start on every piece. Not to be confused with the Indianapolis & Cincinnati Traction interurban or Indianapolis streetcars.
conflicts: Junction Railroad sale to the CH&I: 2 Jan 1873 (ICC text) vs 2 Jan 1878 (ICC succession table). Decides whether the 1875 Official Guide service (Fowler y on every Hamilton - Indianapolis station) was CH&D-operated; 1873-1892 is drawn for neither company.
Hamilton - Indianapolis completion: ICC 1867; Logan's 1868 directory May 1868; Indiana State Library 1869. Does not affect the drawn 1870 start.
CI&W/B&O trains at Cincinnati: CH&D 5th & Baymiller station presumed until CUT opened 1933 (jjakucyk.com via the CH&D report), but a 1928 B&O excursion from Indianapolis used Central Union Station.
Hamilton - Indianapolis CI&W era: the report recommends 1915-1927 (drawn); the strictest reading of the evidence is 1922 [OPEN] - 1925 [OPEN].
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Open ends - each is the first or last CONFIRMED year, not a known start or end; do not extend without evidence: Cincinnati and Indianapolis Junction Hamilton - Indianapolis 1870 [OPEN] - 1872 [OPEN]; Indianapolis, Decatur and Springfield Bruin - Decatur 1878 [OPEN] - 1884 [OPEN] and Indianapolis - Bruin 1880 [OPEN] - 1884 [OPEN]; CH&D Hamilton - Indianapolis 1893 [OPEN] - 1906 [OPEN] (CH&D file). One-year anchors (service surely ran wider): I&IC Montezuma - Decatur 1874 (operator presumed); ID&W Indianapolis - Decatur 1893; CH&D Indianapolis - Decatur 1902; CI&W Indianapolis - Decatur 1922 (1921 if Fowler's 1921t is the CI&W's); CI&W Decatur - Springfield 1921 (low-medium); CH&D Ste. Marie - Alliance 1900 (whole Sidell - Olney branch probable, not proven). Unresolved: no CI&W (1915-27) public timetable or 1916-1926 Official Guide page was read; the B&O takeover month in 1927; the IB&W's role with the ID&S into Indianapolis; I&IC vs ID&S for the 1875 Guide; Decatur - Springfield start, 1902-1906 access to Decatur, and end; whether the whole Sidell - Olney branch carried CH&D-operated passengers 1898-1915; no train names found for any era. Alliance IL is located by Fowler milepost only. headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates throughout except where a note derives them.

segments.note: [OPEN START AND OPEN END] Both years are the first and last CONFIRMED years of this company's era, not known beginnings or endings. The Junction Railroad (Indiana charter 15 Feb 1848; merged with the Ohio and Indianapolis 20 Apr 1853; traded as the Cincinnati and Indianapolis Junction) completed Hamilton - Oxford - College Corner - Connersville - Rushville - Indianapolis by 1867-1869 (ICC Val. vol. 135 says 1867; Logan's Indianapolis Directory 1868 says finished to Indianapolis May 1868; the Indiana State Library says 1869 - construction dates, recorded as a conflict, not resolved). 1870: Fowler IN 71 shows Vienna (Glenwood), Palestine (New Palestine) and Sulphur Springs (Julietta) in the 1870 Official Guide. 1872: Tyner's, Bunker Hill, Gwynne's, Carrolton (Reedville) and Morehouses (Fenton) in the 1872 Guide. The era ends when the Cincinnati, Hamilton and Indianapolis took the property at foreclosure - 2 Jan 1873 in the ICC text but 2 Jan 1878 in the ICC succession table; until that is settled nothing after 1872 is drawn for this company. That the C&IJ itself ran the trains is presumed (the ICC gives no operating statement). Service certainly ran wider both ways - do not extend without evidence. headway_min 720 is a placeholder ESTIMATE; no timetable was read.
sources: Segment-level: Fowler, Indiana Railroads SL 281, line 71, 1870G and 1872G station entries, for both years; ICC Val. vol. 135 for the corporate history and the 1873/1878 conflict; Logan's 1868 directory for construction - as read for research/branches/cincinnati_indianapolis_and_western_railroad.txt (researched 2026-10-30). The operator is presumed and the headway is an estimate.

segments.note: The Cincinnati, Indianapolis and Western RAILROAD (incorporated 30 Oct 1915 after the 9 Sept 1915 foreclosure of the CI&W Railway) ran its own trains from 1 Dec 1915 (ICC Val. vol. 135: operated "by its own organization"); the CH&D had run them before. USRA federal control 1 Jan 1918 - 1 Mar 1920 is not treated as a split. Passenger evidence: the ICC valuation (c.1918) lists 25.37 mi of Toledo and Cincinnati track Hamilton - Cincinnati "used for passenger service only", which can only have carried trains off this line; Indiana Daily Times 22 June 1922 p.3, a railroad advertisement "C., I. & W. EXCURSIONS EVERY SUNDAY ... Rushville, $1.19 ... Connersville, $1.72. Good on All Trains ... Leave Indianapolis 6:10 a.m., 10:40 a.m., 2:35 p.m., 5:10 p.m." (four daily Indianapolis departures; checked to be separate from the adjacent Indianapolis & Cincinnati Traction interurban ad); 14 million passenger-miles system-wide in 1925 (Wikipedia). The Indianapolis Times "Rushville and Connersville Division" schedules are the TRACTION company, not the CI&W. END 1927: the Baltimore and Ohio acquired the road in 1927 (month not established; B&O bought a majority of the stock from Jan 1926 but the Indianapolis Times of 19 Jan 1926 expected the CI&W to keep its separate identity). The B&O feature (bo-hamilton-indianapolis) also starts 1927. The strictest reading of the evidence is 1922 [OPEN] - 1925 [OPEN]; the report recommends 1915-1927 and that is drawn. headway_min 240 is an ESTIMATE from the four Indianapolis departures in the 1922 ad; no CI&W public timetable was read.
sources: Segment-level: ICC Val. vol. 135 for the 1 Dec 1915 start and the passenger-only Hamilton - Cincinnati trackage; Indiana Daily Times 22 June 1922 p.3 (CI&W excursion ad, four departures); Wikipedia CI&W for 1925 passenger-miles and the 1927 B&O acquisition; Indianapolis Times 19 Jan 1926 p.1 for the B&O stock purchase - as read for research/branches/cincinnati_indianapolis_and_western_railroad.txt (researched 2026-10-30). No CI&W timetable was read; the 1927 month is not established; the headway is an estimate.

segments.note: CI&W Railroad passenger trains over the Toledo and Cincinnati (B&O-operated from 18 July 1917; CH&D before) between Hamilton and Cincinnati via Glendale, Lockland and Winton Place. properties.speed_source: Derived from Indianapolis Times 31 Aug 1922 (No. 10: Indianapolis 6:45 a.m. - Decatur 11:57 a.m., 152.7 Fowler miles = ~47 km/h); one train, one year - treat as approximate. Rule 3.
properties.geometry_source: Identical geometry to bo-indianapolis-decatur in cincinnati_hamilton_and_dayton_railway.geojson (OpenStreetMap ways tagged old_railway_operator=B&O via the maps.mail.ru Overpass mirror, routed with opstrace.py, 2026-10-29). Re-traced independently with opstrace.py on 2026-10-30 and compared: same 152.2 mi, mean separation 3 m, worst 167 m on a yard throat; the existing geometry was kept so the Rule 4 ownership-split features share it exactly.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced end to end, no straight-line legs: 152.2 mi drawn against 152.7 mi documented (Fowler IN 72 / IL 147: Indianapolis 0.0 - Decatur 152.7; ICC Val. vol. 135 ~152 mi) - within 0.4%. ~149 mi on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=B&O: the live Decatur Subdivision (Decatur - Hillsdale IN), the lifted grade and the B&O Trail rail-trail (Hendricks County); ~3 mi untagged rail at the ends. Drawn mileposts: Speedway 4.7 (Fowler 4.6), Guion 51.8 (51.8), Montezuma 67.0 (67.2), Chrisman 84.0 (Fowler 84.3), Tuscola 116.6, Decatur 152.2. Ends 0.4 km from Indianapolis Union Station and 0.9 km from Decatur's centre (Decatur station site not pinned). ALIGNMENT ERA: lifted sections follow the mapped grade, which is the line's only alignment.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] One proven year only. Indianapolis Times 31 Aug 1922 p.2, "SERVICE RESUMED": the CI&W announced that trains Nos. 10 and 11, "operating between Indianapolis and Decatur, on the Springfield division", discontinued during the 1922 shopmen's strike, would be restored 4 and 5 Sept - No. 10 lv Indianapolis 6:45 a.m., ar Decatur 11:57; No. 11 lv Decatur 5:00 a.m., ar Indianapolis 10:25 a.m. (a few weeks' suspension, not drawn as a gap). Service certainly ran wider (CI&W own operation 1 Dec 1915 - 1927), but no other year is confirmed on this line: Fowler IL 147's "Springfield 1921t" would make it 1921 [OPEN] - 1922 [OPEN] only if that 1921 timetable is the CI&W's, and the 1925 passenger-miles are system-wide. Do not widen without a timetable. headway_min 1440 = one train each way (Nos. 10/11); avg_speed_kmh 47 is derived from No. 10's 5 h 12 min over 152.7 mi.
sources: Segment-level: Indianapolis Times 31 Aug 1922 p.2 for trains 10/11 and their times; Fowler IL 147 for the 1921t alternative; ICC Val. vol. 135 for the CI&W operating dates - as read for research/branches/cincinnati_indianapolis_and_western_railroad.txt (researched 2026-10-30). Only one 1922 article; no CI&W timetable was read.

properties.line: Cincinnati, Indianapolis and Western: Decatur – Springfield
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE - not taken from a timetable; no end-to-end running time was read for this era. Rule 3.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via the maps.mail.ru Overpass mirror, routed with opstrace.py 2026-10-30: NS Brooklyn District (old_railway_operator=Wabash) Decatur - Boody, then the lifted B&O grade (way "B&O Decatur Sub", railway=abandoned/razed, old_railway_operator=B&O) Boody - Springfield, with the Lost Bridge Trail rail-trail alongside it at Springfield; starts at the Decatur end of bo-indianapolis-decatur.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced end to end, no straight-line legs: 41.9 mi drawn against 44.5 mi documented (ICC Val. vol. 135: 8.49 Wabash trackage + 26.00 Boody - Derry Farm + 7.52 Derry Farm - Springfield + 2.54 C&A trackage; Fowler IL 147 Decatur 152.7 - Springfield 197.3 = 44.6) - about 6% short. ~41 mi on ways tagged old_railway_operator=Wabash or B&O, ~1 mi untagged rail into the Springfield (ex-Chicago & Alton) station. Drawn mileposts from Decatur against Fowler: Boody 8.8 (8.3), Mount Auburn 19.8 (19.7), Bolivia 24.7 (24.3), Roby 27.9 (27.1), Buckhart 29.5 (29.7); Derry Farm ~34.8 (34.5). The whole shortfall is the Springfield approach: 7.1 mi drawn Derry Farm - Springfield against 10.06 mi documented (7.52 own + 2.54 C&A) - OSM maps the B&O grade straight west into town and ends it ~1.8 km east of the C&A station; how the CI&W joined the C&A (East Springfield, Fowler 193.2) is not mapped, so the last mile follows modern untagged track. The Boody junction and Decatur terminal approach are the post-1906 Wabash trackage route; the Decatur station used is not pinned.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] One proven year only, LOW-MEDIUM confidence. Fowler IL 147 lists "Springfield (CA/GMO) 1921t" - the Chicago & Alton station at Springfield in a 1921 company public timetable, on the CI&W's own station list; the CI&W reached it over C&A trackage under a 25 Sept 1902 agreement (ICC Val. vol. 135). That the 1921 timetable is the CI&W's is the report's reading, not certain. CAUTION: in 1922 trains Nos. 10/11 ran only Indianapolis - Decatur although the line was called the "Springfield division" (Indianapolis Times 31 Aug 1922) - whether any train ran on to Springfield then is unproven either way. Built 1901-1902 (Springfield and Decatur Ry / ID&W); trains reached Decatur over the Wabash Decatur - Boody under a 1 Feb 1906 agreement. Neither the CH&D era (1902-1915) nor the B&O era has a confirmed passenger year and neither is drawn; the Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 60 shows the line freight-only by 1951. The 1984 Springfield - Boody abandonment (cs.trains.com, unread) is not a passenger date. Service certainly ran wider - do not widen without a timetable. headway_min 1440 is a placeholder ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: Fowler IL 147 ("Springfield (CA/GMO) 1921t") for the anchor year; ICC Val. vol. 135 for construction and the Wabash/C&A trackage; Indianapolis Times 31 Aug 1922 for the caution - as read for research/branches/cincinnati_indianapolis_and_western_railroad.txt (researched 2026-10-30). Low-medium confidence; the headway is an estimate.

properties.line: Cincinnati, Hamilton and Dayton: Ste. Marie – Alliance
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE - not taken from a timetable; no end-to-end running time was read for this era. Rule 3.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via the maps.mail.ru Overpass mirror plus OpenHistoricalMap: the lifted Danville, Olney and Ohio River grade, tagged old_railway_operator="Kansas and Sidell" (OSM) and named "Kansas and Sidell Railroad" (OHM); routed Willow Hill - Ste. Marie - West Liberty with opstrace.py 2026-10-30 and cut to the drawn span.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced, no straight-line legs: 1.6 mi drawn against 1.6 mi documented (Fowler IL 211: Ste. Marie 70.4 - Alliance 72). Willow Hill - Ste. Marie - West Liberty traced 9.7 mi on the K&S-tagged grade against 11.1 mi in Fowler (65.9 - 77.0), about 13% short; the OSM way carries a "rough alignment in places" FIXME. ALLIANCE IS NOT GEOCODED (no Nominatim or OSM place): its end is placed 1.6 mi along the traced grade from Ste. Marie toward West Liberty, by Fowler's milepost alone. The grade was built 3 ft gauge (DO&OR) and later standard-gauged; the mapped grade is the only alignment recorded.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] One proven year, on one short piece only. The Danville, Olney and Ohio River (Sidell - Kansas - Casey - Willow Hill - Ste. Marie - West Liberty - Olney, built 3 ft gauge) was acquired by the Indianapolis, Decatur and Western 16 Dec 1898 and operated by the CH&D as agent (later for the CI&W Railway) until the 9 Sept 1915 foreclosure, when it went to the Sidell & Olney (ICC Val. vol. 135). Fowler IL 211 shows "St. Marie 1900G" and "Alliance 1900G" - the 1900 Official Guide - and gives no 1900 letter north of Ste. Marie, so only Ste. Marie - Alliance is drawn. The whole branch Sidell - Olney probably carried CH&D-operated passengers 1898-1915 (likely mixed trains), but that is not proven - do not extend along the branch or across years without evidence. The DO&OR's own 1881 anchor and the Sidell & Olney / Kansas & Sidell 1926 Sidell - Kansas anchor belong to other companies' rows and are not drawn here; the Sidell & Olney was CI&W-owned by stock but "operated separately" (ICC) and must not take CI&W colour. headway_min 1440 is a placeholder ESTIMATE.

The headway is an estimate.
